Documents' with one task, 'Upload documents', linking to the page; it shows 'To do' while no document has been added and 'Complete' once documents are saved. requirements.statement: Each document is saved to the notification as soon as it is added, as its own record in the backend's accompanying_documents collection keyed by the notification reference, with its type code, reference, date of issue as a YYYY-MM-DD date, a UUID upload id, scan status and files; it is still listed on a fresh load, and a retried save or removal does not add or remove it twice.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps documents in the session and only saves the draft on some buttons. Storing them durably is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend keeps each document in accompanying_documents linked by notification reference, with a unique upload id and a YYYY-MM-DD date (repo-backend-p3-016, repo-backend-p3-017, repo-backend-p3-021); a repeated claim never makes a second document (repo-backend-p3-048); repo-tests-p5-079 and trace-e2e-p14-148 show each document still listed after a reload.

requirements.statement: The browser posts the add form and its file straight to cdp-uploader's upload-and-scan address, so the file never passes through the frontend or the backend. Each time the page is drawn the frontend opens a cdp-uploader session limited to 50MB and the eight accepted file types and registers it with the backend against the notification. cdp-uploader scans the file, keeps a clean file in the documents S3 bucket, reports the result to the backend's scan-result callback, matched by correlation id, and returns the browser to the page, which then gives the backend the document's type, reference and date of issue. A document becomes COMPLETE only when no file was rejected (fail closed). A failure to use the uploader shows 'The selected file could not be uploaded. Try again.', and a failure to reach it at all brings the page back as a service failure with the details the trader typed still in the form. In CDP the scan is the real cdp-uploader; on the local stack it is the stack's cdp-uploader container with a mock scan.
requirements.why: This is the real upload handshake behind the page; Design Release 2.1 sends only the filename and cannot express it.
requirements.deltaNote: The frontend opens and registers a session per render and posts the form straight to cdp-uploader (repo-frontend-p17-134, repo-frontend-p17-139, repo-backend-p3-033, repo-backend-p3-083, repo-perftests-p3-042), then claims the document with an ISO date (repo-frontend-p17-136, repo-backend-p3-046); the scan callback fails closed (repo-backend-p3-058). The earlier traces that show the file posted to the frontend (trace-e2e-p12-073, trace-animals-fit-p22-080) were captured before this direct upload. The backend keeps upload sessions unique by uploadId and correlationId, validates both, refuses a duplicate registration, finds a session only by notification and correlationId together, refuses a scan result with no or an unknown correlationId, records the file details cdp-uploader reports, and holds a scanned document unclaimed with no type, reference or date until the trader claims it (repo-backend-p3-020 to repo-backend-p3-071).

requirements.statement: Documents can be added, listed and removed whatever the notification's status, draft, submitted or in amendment; they are deleted with their notification; and only documents that scanned clean are referenced in the events the backend publishes.
requirements.why: These are the cross-service rules around the document record; the design does not contradict them, and amending a notification reaches the page in Design Release 2.1 too.
requirements.deltaNote: A claim does not check the notification's status (repo-backend-p3-051), documents and sessions are deleted with their notification and share its expiry (repo-backend-p3-087, repo-backend-p3-088), and only claimed COMPLETE documents go on the published event (repo-backend-p3-089), over the four notification statuses repo-tests-p5-062 names. Every document endpoint but the scan callback checks the notification belongs to the calling organisation (repo-backend-p3-039).

requirements.statement: The documents page stays safe and recoverable: text the trader typed is HTML-escaped in table cells; a row with no reference or date of issue reads 'Not provided'; a failed delete of an upload leaves the document in place; and a saved document whose type or attachment type the service no longer lists raises 'One or more of your saved documents are no longer valid. Review the list before you continue.'.
requirements.why: Real-service safeguards with no design counterpart; Design Release 2.1 does not contradict them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-060, repo-frontend-p17-077, repo-frontend-p17-091 and repo-frontend-p18-010 hold these safeguards today.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-086 leaves an untouched form alone, and repo-tests-p5-063 submits a notification with no fulfilments at all.

requirements.statement: Backend document-endpoint defects: the scan callback is unauthenticated; deleting a document leaves its file in S3; the list has no defined order; a notification of another organisation is answered 404 where the API description says 403; the Location header a registration returns points at an address that answers 404 until the document is written; the get, delete and download endpoints check no pattern on the upload id; and a document whose 24-hour upload session has expired can no longer be read, downloaded, deleted or claimed.

Organisation scoping is no longer a defect: every endpoint but the scan callback checks the notification's organisation (repo-backend-p3-039).

requirements.statement: A document whose file was taken on but not saved to the notification is recoverable: the page returns with 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your document was uploaded but has not been saved to this notification. Select <save action> to try again.', or with 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. We could not check that every document you uploaded is saved to this notification. Select <save action> to try again.' when the service cannot be asked, and holds the trader on the page until the outstanding upload or removal is finished. A page shown after a service failure carries an internal-server-error status, and one shown after a refused add or continue a bad-request status.

requirements.statement: Each time the documents page is drawn the add control posts to a fresh upload session, a page the browser restored from its back or forward store is reopened from the service, and the page is served with no-store, so the add control never posts to a session that has already taken a file and a trader who comes back by Back can still add another document.
requirements.why: A one-use upload session is how the real upload handshake works, which the prototype cannot express; without this a trader returning to a stale page would post a second file to a spent session.
